I didn't really like it either. I think it was because the way they set up the story forced them to spend time on things other than the problem of AI, and it ended up not being a satisfactory exploration of the topic. Plus, the protagonist was an idiot and I didn't empathize with him at all, and the mysterious genius really grated on me.

I think they set up the story pretty well and it was actually a really well done film because it felt like an actual film. It told it's story through images and simply placed characters on the screen so that the plot could move through them. I think it was shot with a great style. As for the story, I don't think it was very good but it was simple enough so that it made sense and very fluid. I'm not sure where they could go in the field of A.I. but it definitely explores the topic much further than any other film has done in the genre that I've seen. Could they have explored the topic further? Absolutely. But in doing so they would have sacrificed the core of what makes a film. It'd force dialogue consisting of extreme amounts of exposition which turns a film into a novel and I was not interested in the film because I felt like reading.

Eh, I'm not talking about teaching the viewer about AI, I'm talking about asking more interesting questions about AI, which I feel they could have done if they picked less of a weird setting, and maybe hadn't implicitly given us the assumption that this machine is an authentic AI by giving it human form. I feel like that's not even the biggest part of why I was so unsatisfied by the movie though. I think it was because the characters made bad decisions, or at least decisions that I wouldn't have made.

I can understand that, there's definitely a thought that art should introduce questions rather than attempting to answer them. I agree they probably could have done better in that regard. However I think limitations on the current state of AI development probably created roadblocks in the kind of questions we can ask. I think the reasoning behind giving it human form was more so done for the attraction element and people wanting to see people on screen, rather than literal AI. I do feel that this was a movie that could start a narrative on AI in the mainstream and could help discussion gain traction as a topic of art because it was a well done film stylistically. I agree that the character elements were a definite weak point especially with the main protagonist but I think they did well with the other characters in the film. The protagonist made decisions that were absolutely idiotic and made no sense on any level beyond empathy and that could be a problem that you may have had with the film. In any case however I still believe that the cinematography for the film was fantastic and told the narrative very well and clearly through it's imagery and held up most of the slack that was created by the poorly written characters.
